howItWorks.heading: How WPM is Calculated
howItWorks.formulaDesc: In standard typing measurement, one 'word' is standardized as 5 keystrokes (including letters, spaces, and punctuation). This ensures fair comparison regardless of word length.
howItWorks.formulaText:
Gross WPM = (Total Typed Characters ÷ 5) ÷ Elapsed Minutes
Net WPM = (Correct Characters ÷ 5) ÷ Elapsed Minutes
Accuracy = (Correct Characters ÷ Total Typed Characters) × 100%
CPM = Correct Characters ÷ Elapsed Minutes
howItWorks.accuracyDesc: Our engine computes Net WPM directly from correctly typed characters. Incorrect keystrokes reduce your overall accuracy percentage and do not contribute to your Net WPM.

faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subheading: Common questions about typing test measurement, WPM calculation, and practice methodology.

items.q: What is a good typing speed?
items.a: For most everyday computer use and general office tasks, 45–60 WPM is a productive, comfortable speed. Specialized roles such as live customer support or data entry often seek 60+ WPM with 95%+ accuracy. Actual requirements vary by employer and specific role.

items.q: How can I increase my WPM?
items.a: Focus first on tactile finger placement from the home row (F and J anchors). Practice with short, consistent typing sessions rather than lengthy, tiring drills. Reviewing mistake trends helps you address difficult letter transitions.

items.q: How does accuracy affect Net WPM?
items.a: Gross WPM measures your total keystroke rate. Net WPM measures only correctly typed characters: (Correct Characters ÷ 5) ÷ Elapsed Minutes. Uncorrected mistakes do not count toward Net WPM, while correcting errors with backspace takes extra time.

items.q: How is WPM different from CPM?
items.a: WPM (Words Per Minute) groups characters into standard 5-character words. CPM (Characters Per Minute) counts every individual correct character per minute. Mathematically in our engine, CPM = Net WPM × 5.

items.q: Can I practice in Hindi, Spanish, or other languages?
items.a: Yes. You can paste custom text in any Unicode language into the custom test engine or upload a .txt file. The engine calculates WPM, CPM, and accuracy using the same 5-character standardized measurement.
